objects.description: Intrusive singly linked list node used to store arbitrary byte-strings (often DNS-SD TXT records). Each node carries the length in size and a flexible trailing data array in text (declared as size 1 for C89 compatibility). Lists are stored in reverse order to make append operations O(1) by prepending. An empty list is represented by a NULL pointer. Memory management is handled by the Avahi string list API; callers typically create via the avahi_string_list_new/… functions and must free with avahi_string_list_free. Note: text may contain NUL bytes; many helper APIs treat entries as either raw byte strings or NUL-terminated strings depending on the function used.

objects.definition: typedef int AvahiProtocol;
objects.description: Protocol family specifier for Avahi addresses. Values are given by the anonymous enum constants AVAHI_PROTO_INET, AVAHI_PROTO_INET6, and AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC.

objects.definition: typedef int AvahiIfIndex;
objects.description: OS-dependent numeric network interface index. May be AVAHI_IF_UNSPEC to indicate an unspecified/all interfaces selection.
Holds an IPv4 address in network byte order.
Holds an IPv6 address as 16 bytes.
Protocol-independent IP address container. The proto field selects IPv4 or IPv6; the union stores the address accordingly or as raw bytes up to IPv6 size.
Enumerates lifecycle states of an Avahi server object, used to track when the daemon is registering, running, in collision, or failed.
States for an entry group, indicating commit/registration progress, collisions, or failure.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_UNIQUE = 1,           /**< For raw records: The RRset is intended to be unique */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_NO_PROBE = 2,         /**< For raw records: Though the RRset is intended to be unique no probes shall be sent */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_NO_ANNOUNCE = 4,      /**< For raw records: Do not announce this RR to other hosts */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_ALLOW_MULTIPLE = 8,   /**< For raw records: Allow multiple local records of this type, even if they are intended to be unique */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_NO_REVERSE = 16,      /**< For address records: don't create a reverse (PTR) entry */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_NO_COOKIE = 32,       /**< For service records: do not implicitly add the local service cookie to TXT data */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_UPDATE = 64,          /**< Update existing records instead of adding new ones */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_USE_WIDE_AREA = 128,  /**< Register the record using wide area DNS (i.e. unicast DNS update) */
    AVAHI_PUBLISH_USE_MULTICAST = 256   /**< Register the record using multicast DNS */
} AvahiPublishFlags;
objects.description: Bitmask flags controlling publishing behavior for records and services (uniqueness, probing, announcements, reverse PTR, cookies, update vs add, and wide-area vs multicast).
Bitmask flags controlling lookup/resolution behavior (transport selection and whether to fetch TXT or address records).
Bitmask flags describing properties of lookup results (source and ownership of data).
Event type passed to browse callbacks indicating discovered, removed, cache boundaries, or errors.
Event type for resolver callbacks indicating success or failure.
Specifies what kind of domain list to browse (browsing domains, registering domains, defaults, or legacy).

Allocator vtable that lets callers override Avahi's memory allocation functions. Each field is a function pointer corresponding to malloc, free, realloc, and calloc. The calloc pointer may be NULL. The struct is used by avahi_set_allocator() to change the active allocator; the passed instance is not copied and must remain valid for as long as it is in use.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiWatch AvahiWatch;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared handle for an I/O watch registered with an AvahiPoll provider. Represents interest in specific file-descriptor events. No fields are exposed here; lifecycle is managed through the AvahiPoll function pointers (watch_new/update/get_events/free).

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiTimeout AvahiTimeout;
objects.description: Opaque forward-declared handle for a timeout event registered with an AvahiPoll provider. Represents a scheduled callback at or after a specified absolute timeval. Lifecycle is managed through the AvahiPoll function pointers (timeout_new/update/free).

Provider vtable for integrating Avahi with an external main loop. Contains userdata and function pointers to create/update/query/free I/O watches and create/update/free timeouts. Implementations supply these callbacks; consumers call through them.
Bitmask-like enum mapping to poll(2) event flags used to express interest and to report readiness or errors for AvahiWatch instances. Values mirror POLLIN, POLLOUT, POLLERR, POLLHUP.

objects.definition: typedef int64_t AvahiUsec;
objects.description: Alias for a signed 64-bit integer used to represent time intervals in microseconds. Intended for use with timeval helper APIs in this header. Construction and destruction are trivial as it is a typedef of a fundamental integer type.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiSimplePoll AvahiSimplePoll;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a simple poll()-based main loop used by Avahi. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure layout is hidden. It supports basic event iteration, quitting, wakeup, and integrating with AvahiPoll.

objects.definition: typedef int (*AvahiPollFunc)(struct pollfd *ufds, unsigned int nfds, int timeout, void *userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type matching a poll()-like routine used by AvahiSimplePoll. Allows substituting the underlying polling implementation. Parameters mirror poll(): array of pollfd, count, timeout in ms, and user data; returns an int like poll().

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiThreadedPoll AvahiThreadedPoll;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a threaded main-loop object that runs an AvahiSimplePoll in its own helper thread. The struct is forward-declared only; implementation is hidden. Use the provided API to create, start/stop the thread, lock/unlock, and destroy. Details of internal fields are unknown from this header.

No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file only declares preprocessor macros for GCC attributes and includes C linkage macros. There are no forward declarations or type aliases present.

objects.definition: const char *avahi_strerror(int error);
objects.description: Function returning a human-readable string for an Avahi error code. Not a type; included here only to note that it produces a const char pointer. No constructors apply.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiRList AvahiRList;
objects.description: Opaque type alias for the AvahiRList struct representing a node in a doubly linked list. Provides a forward declaration used by APIs that manipulate the list before the full struct definition.

Node of a simple doubly linked list. Each node contains linkage fields injected by AVAHI_LLIST_FIELDS(AvahiRList, rlist) macro (presumably next/prev pointers) and a void* payload 'data'. Used with avahi_rlist_* functions for list manipulation. Exact linkage members depend on llist.h macro expansion and are not shown here.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiClient AvahiClient;
objects.description: Opaque client connection context to the Avahi daemon over D-Bus. Only a forward declaration is provided here; the structure layout is hidden. Constructed and managed via the avahi_client_* API. Lifetime is controlled by avahi_client_new()/avahi_client_free().

Enumeration of Avahi client states (a superset of AvahiServerState). Values mirror server states for registering/running/collision and add FAILURE and CONNECTING for client-side errors and deferred connection behavior.
Bitmask flags that modify Avahi client behavior at creation time (e.g., ignore user config, tolerate missing daemon and enter CONNECTING).

objects.definition:
typedef void (*AvahiClientCallback) (
    AvahiClient *s,
    AvahiClientState state,
    void* userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type for client state change callbacks invoked by the client library. Receives the AvahiClient instance, the new AvahiClientState, and the user-supplied pointer.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiDomainBrowser AvahiDomainBrowser;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a domain browser used to discover browsing, registration, or browsing default domains via the Avahi client API. Only forward-declared here; implementation is private.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*AvahiDomainBrowserCallback) (
    AvahiDomainBrowser *b,
    AvahiIfIndex interface,
    AvahiProtocol protocol,
    AvahiBrowserEvent event,
    const char *domain,
    AvahiLookupResultFlags flags,
    void *userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type invoked by AvahiDomainBrowser to deliver domain browse events. Called with interface/protocol, event type, domain string, result flags, and user data.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiServiceBrowser AvahiServiceBrowser;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a service browser that discovers DNS-SD services of a given type and domain.
Function pointer type invoked by AvahiServiceBrowser to report service appearance/removal and related metadata.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiServiceTypeBrowser AvahiServiceTypeBrowser;
objects.description: Opaque handle used to browse available service types in a domain. Forward-declared only.
Function pointer type for callbacks from AvahiServiceTypeBrowser delivering service type browse events.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiServiceResolver AvahiServiceResolver;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a resolver that looks up full details (host, address, port, TXT) for a specific service instance.
Function pointer type invoked by AvahiServiceResolver to deliver resolution results including host, address, port, and TXT data.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiHostNameResolver AvahiHostNameResolver;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a resolver that maps a host name to one or more addresses.
Function pointer type invoked by AvahiHostNameResolver to deliver hostname-to-address resolution results.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiAddressResolver AvahiAddressResolver;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a resolver that maps an address to a host name (reverse lookup).
Function pointer type invoked by AvahiAddressResolver to deliver reverse DNS results mapping an address to a host name.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiRecordBrowser AvahiRecordBrowser;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a browser for arbitrary DNS records identified by name, class, and type.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*AvahiRecordBrowserCallback) (
    AvahiRecordBrowser *b,
    AvahiIfIndex interface,
    AvahiProtocol protocol,
    AvahiBrowserEvent event,
    const char *name,
    uint16_t clazz,
    uint16_t type,
    const void *rdata,
    size_t size,
    AvahiLookupResultFlags flags,
    void *userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type invoked by AvahiRecordBrowser to deliver record browse events with raw rdata and size.

objects.definition: typedef struct AvahiEntryGroup AvahiEntryGroup;
objects.description: Opaque handle to an entry group used to batch and manage DNS-SD records (services, addresses, arbitrary records) published via an AvahiClient. The actual struct is not defined here; it is managed by the Avahi client library. Entry groups are created, committed, reset, and freed through the provided API functions.

objects.definition:
typedef void (*AvahiEntryGroupCallback) (
    AvahiEntryGroup *g,
    AvahiEntryGroupState state,
    void* userdata);
objects.description: Function pointer type for callbacks invoked on AvahiEntryGroup state changes. Receives the group, the new AvahiEntryGroupState, and the user-provided context pointer. AvahiEntryGroupState is declared elsewhere and not defined in this header.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_new
functions.description: Create a new AvahiStringList from a variable list of NUL-terminated strings. Strings are copied (per docs: using g_strdup()). The argument list must end with a NULL sentinel. The resulting list is stored in reverse order (appending is prepending). Pass NULL for an empty list.
requirements: Each argument must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
The variable argument list must be terminated by a NULL pointer (sentinel).
Callers may pass no strings (i.e., first argument NULL) to construct an empty list (represented as NULL).
Returned list head must be used for subsequent operations since appending prepends internally.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_new_va
functions.description: Create a new AvahiStringList from a va_list of NUL-terminated strings. Equivalent to avahi_string_list_new() but takes a va_list.
requirements: The va_list must contain pointers to NUL-terminated strings and be terminated by a NULL pointer sentinel.
The va_list must be properly initialized by the caller and used in a valid lifetime/scope.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_new_from_array
functions.description: Create a new AvahiStringList from an array of NUL-terminated strings. Strings are copied. If length is -1, the array must be NULL-terminated.
requirements: array must point to an array of pointers to NUL-terminated strings.
If length is -1, the array must be terminated with a NULL pointer.
If length is non-negative, it specifies the number of entries to read; the function will not rely on a NULL terminator.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_free
functions.description: Free a string list and all associated storage.
requirements: l should be either NULL (empty list) or a valid AvahiStringList head pointer allocated by this API.
After calling, the pointer must not be used again.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add
functions.description: Append a NUL-terminated string to the list (implemented as prepending to the linked list). The string is copied. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
text must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_printf
functions.description: Append a formatted NUL-terminated string to the list (printf-style). The resulting string is copied. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; subsequent varargs must match the format.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_vprintf
functions.description: Append a formatted NUL-terminated string to the list using a va_list. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
format must be a valid printf-style format string; the va_list must supply matching arguments.
va_list must be properly initialized and valid for reading during the call.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_arbitrary
functions.description: Append an arbitrary-length byte string (may contain NUL bytes) to the list. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
text must point to at least size bytes of data (may contain NULs).
size specifies the exact number of bytes to copy.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_anonymous
functions.description: Append a new entry of a given size without initializing its content. Intended to avoid extra copying; the caller should write the data directly to the returned node’s text buffer (node->text). Returns the new list head (the new node).
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
size specifies the length of the new entry’s text buffer.
After the call, the caller should write at most size bytes to the returned node’s text (returned->text).
Do not read from the new entry’s text until the caller has populated it.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_many
functions.description: Append multiple NUL-terminated strings in one call. The argument list must be terminated by a NULL pointer. Returns the new list head.
requirements: r may be NULL to represent an empty list.
All provided arguments must be valid NUL-terminated strings.
The variable argument list must be terminated by a NULL sentinel.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_many_va
functions.description: Append multiple NUL-terminated strings provided via a va_list. Returns the new list head.
requirements: r may be NULL to represent an empty list.
va_list must contain pointers to NUL-terminated strings and be terminated by a NULL pointer sentinel.
va_list must be properly initialized and valid for reading.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_to_string
functions.description: Convert the list to a single human-readable character string with items separated by spaces and enclosed in quotes. Not suitable for items containing NUL bytes. The caller must avahi_free() the returned string.
requirements: l may be NULL (resulting in a valid representation of an empty list; exact output format unspecified).
The returned buffer must be freed with avahi_free() by the caller.
Do not rely on this for elements containing NUL bytes; result may be incorrect.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_serialize
functions.description: Serialize the list to a buffer in a format compatible with DNS TXT records. Individual strings longer than 255 bytes are truncated. Returns the number of bytes written (and/or required, typical for serializers; exact return semantics not fully documented here).
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes when non-NULL.
Strings longer than 255 bytes will be truncated during serialization.
Caller must provide adequate buffer size to avoid truncation beyond the per-string 255-byte limit (overall size requirements depend on list contents).

functions.name: avahi_string_list_parse
functions.signature: int avahi_string_list_parse(const void *data, size_t size, AvahiStringList **ret);
functions.description: Parse a DNS TXT record-compatible buffer into an AvahiStringList (inverse of avahi_string_list_serialize). On success, stores the resulting list in *ret.
requirements: data must point to size bytes of serialized TXT record data.
ret must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the resulting list head; the caller is responsible for freeing it with avahi_string_list_free().
size must match the actual length of the buffer pointed to by data.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_equal
functions.description: Compare two string lists for equality.
requirements: a and b may be NULL (empty lists).

functions.name: avahi_string_list_copy
functions.description: Create a deep copy of a string list.
requirements: l may be NULL (result is NULL).
Caller must free the returned list with avahi_string_list_free().

functions.name: avahi_string_list_reverse
functions.description: Reverse the order of elements in the list. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL.
Use the returned list head after the call.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_length
functions.description: Return the number of elements in the list.
requirements: l may be NULL (length is 0).

functions.name: avahi_string_list_get_next
functions.description: Return the next item in the list (i.e., l->next).
requirements: l must be a valid pointer to a list node (non-NULL).

functions.name: avahi_string_list_get_text
functions.description: Return a pointer to the data bytes (text) for the current list item. The data may contain NUL bytes.
requirements: l must be a valid pointer to a list node (non-NULL).
The returned pointer is only valid as long as the node remains valid and unmodified.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_get_size
functions.description: Return the size in bytes of the current item’s text.
requirements: l must be a valid pointer to a list node (non-NULL).

functions.name: avahi_string_list_find
functions.description: Find the list entry corresponding to the given DNS-SD TXT key.
requirements: l may be NULL.
key must be a valid NUL-terminated string representing a DNS-SD TXT key.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_get_pair
functions.description: Extract the DNS-SD TXT key and value from the current list item. If size is not NULL, it receives the length of value (useful when value contains NUL bytes). If the entry has no value, *value is set to NULL. The caller must avahi_free() the strings stored into *key and *value.
requirements: l must be a valid pointer to a list node (non-NULL).
key must be a non-NULL pointer to char* for receiving an allocated string; caller must free it with avahi_free().
value must be a non-NULL pointer to char* for receiving an allocated string or NULL; caller must free it with avahi_free() when non-NULL.
size may be NULL; if non-NULL, it will be set to the value length.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_pair
functions.description: Add a DNS-SD TXT key/value pair to the list. value may be NULL to indicate a key without a value. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
key must be a valid NUL-terminated string (DNS-SD TXT key).
value may be NULL or a valid NUL-terminated string.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_add_pair_arbitrary
functions.signature: AvahiStringList *avahi_string_list_add_pair_arbitrary(AvahiStringList *l, const char *key, const uint8_t *value, size_t size);
functions.description: Add a DNS-SD TXT key with a value that may contain NUL bytes. Returns the new list head.
requirements: l may be NULL to represent an empty list.
key must be a valid NUL-terminated string (DNS-SD TXT key).
If value is non-NULL, it must point to at least size bytes; size gives the exact length of the value.
Use the returned list head for further operations.

functions.name: avahi_string_list_get_service_cookie
functions.description: Search the list for a magic service cookie and return it, or AVAHI_SERVICE_COOKIE_INVALID if none is found.
requirements: l may be NULL.

functions.name: avahi_address_cmp
functions.description: Compares two AvahiAddress values. Returns 0 when equal, a negative value when a < b, and a positive value when a > b. Intended for ordering and equality checks across IPv4/IPv6 addresses based on their protocol and address bytes.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to an initialized AvahiAddress.
b must be a non-null pointer to an initialized AvahiAddress.
The proto field of each address should be a valid AvahiProtocol (AVAHI_PROTO_INET, AVAHI_PROTO_INET6, or AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC).
Callers should use the integer return to determine ordering or equality (0 means equal).

functions.name: avahi_address_snprint
functions.description: Formats the AvahiAddress a as a human-readable string into ret_s. Use AVAHI_ADDRESS_STR_MAX (40) as a safe maximum buffer size for IPv6 textual representation.
requirements: ret_s must be a non-null writable buffer.
length must reflect the size of ret_s and should be at least AVAHI_ADDRESS_STR_MAX to hold any IPv6 address plus NUL.
a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized AvahiAddress.
The function writes a NUL-terminated string not exceeding length bytes.
Callers should check the return value (ret_s or possibly NULL on failure; exact failure semantics are not documented).

functions.name: avahi_address_parse
functions.description: Parses a human-readable IP address string s into ret_addr. If af is AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC, the address family is detected automatically (comment uses AVAHI_UNSPEC, which appears to be a typo; the defined constant is AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC). Returns a pointer to the filled AvahiAddress (typically ret_addr).
requirements: s must be a non-null, NUL-terminated C string containing an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
af must be a valid AvahiProtocol; pass AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC to auto-detect the family.
ret_addr must be a non-null pointer to writable AvahiAddress storage.
On failure, the function may return NULL; callers should check the return value before using ret_addr.
The caller must ensure ret_addr remains valid for subsequent use.

functions.name: avahi_reverse_lookup_name
functions.signature: char* avahi_reverse_lookup_name(const AvahiAddress *a, char *ret_s, size_t length);
functions.description: Generates the DNS reverse lookup (PTR) name for the IPv4 or IPv6 address a (e.g., in-addr.arpa for IPv4, ip6.arpa for IPv6) and writes it into ret_s.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to an initialized AvahiAddress with a valid proto and address bytes.
ret_s must be a non-null writable buffer.

length must be sufficient to hold the full reverse name plus NUL; for IPv6 ip6.arpa names, this can be long. The exact maximum is not documented here; callers should provide a generously sized buffer.
Callers should check the return value (likely ret_s on success or NULL on failure; exact failure semantics are not documented).

functions.name: avahi_proto_to_af
functions.description: Maps an AvahiProtocol value (AVAHI_PROTO_INET, AVAHI_PROTO_INET6, or AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC) to the corresponding Unix socket address family constant (e.g., AF_INET, AF_INET6, or an unspecified family).
requirements: proto should be a valid AvahiProtocol constant.
Returned value is a Unix AF_xxx integer; callers should handle the possibility of an unspecified or unsupported mapping (exact error or fallback behavior is not documented).

functions.name: avahi_af_to_proto
functions.description: Maps a Unix socket address family (AF_xxx) to the corresponding AvahiProtocol (AVAHI_PROTO_INET, AVAHI_PROTO_INET6, or AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC).
requirements: af should be a valid Unix AF_xxx value (e.g., AF_INET or AF_INET6).
Callers should handle the case where af is not recognized; the exact return in that case is not documented (could be AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC or another indicator).

functions.name: avahi_proto_to_string
functions.description: Returns a textual representation of an AvahiProtocol value, e.g., "IPv4", "IPv6", or "UNSPEC".
requirements: proto should be a valid AvahiProtocol.
The returned pointer refers to a constant string that must not be modified or freed by the caller.
Callers should be prepared for a NULL or implementation-defined string if proto is invalid (not documented).

functions.name: avahi_alternative_host_name
functions.description: Generate an alternative host name to avoid collisions. If s is an original host name, the function appends "-2"; if s already ends with "-N" (N ≥ 2), it increments N (e.g., "foo" → "foo-2" → "foo-3"). The function returns a newly allocated string; callers must free it with avahi_free(). Typical usage is to call this when a chosen host name is in use, and if the new name also collides, call again with the returned name to advance the suffix.
requirements: s must point to a valid, null-terminated C string (const char*); it must not be NULL (inferred from signature and typical C APIs).
The returned string is heap-allocated and must be released with avahi_free() (explicitly stated).
Do not free the returned string with free(); use avahi_free() (explicitly stated via documentation).

functions.name: avahi_alternative_service_name
functions.description: Generate an alternative service name to avoid collisions. If s is an original service name, the function appends " #2"; if s already ends with " #N" (N ≥ 2), it increments N (e.g., "foo" → "foo #2" → "foo #3"). The function returns a newly allocated string; callers must free it with avahi_free(). Typical usage is to call this when a chosen service name is already in use, and if needed, call again with the returned name to advance the suffix.
requirements: s must point to a valid, null-terminated C string (const char*); it must not be NULL (inferred from signature and typical C APIs).
The returned string is heap-allocated and must be released with avahi_free() (explicitly stated).
Do not free the returned string with free(); use avahi_free() (explicitly stated via documentation).

functions.name: avahi_normalize_name
functions.description: Normalize a domain name into canonical form by dropping trailing dots and removing unnecessary backslash escapes. Writes the normalized name into the provided output buffer and returns it.
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string representing a domain name.
ret_s must be a valid, writable buffer.
size must specify the capacity of ret_s in bytes and be large enough to hold the normalized output including the terminating NUL.
The caller must not pass overlapping input/output buffers unless explicitly supported (not stated here).
The returned pointer is ret_s; it remains owned by the caller.

functions.name: avahi_normalize_name_strdup
functions.description: Normalize a domain name into canonical form by dropping trailing dots and removing unnecessary backslash escapes, returning a newly allocated string. The result must be freed with avahi_free().
requirements: s must be a valid NUL-terminated C string representing a domain name.
The caller must free the returned string with avahi_free().
On allocation failure or invalid input, the function may return NULL (exact error signaling is unknown).

functions.name: avahi_domain_equal
functions.description: Compare two domain names for equality in Avahi’s canonical sense. Returns 1 if equal, 0 otherwise.
requirements: a and b must be valid NUL-terminated C strings representing domain names.
Return value is 1 for equal, 0 for not equal; no other return codes are documented.

functions.name: avahi_domain_hash
functions.description: Compute a hash value for a domain name suitable for use as a hash table key.
requirements: name must be a valid NUL-terminated C string representing a domain name.
The returned hash is an implementation-defined unsigned value; no stability across runs is guaranteed (not stated).

functions.name: avahi_unescape_label
functions.description: Read the first label from the textual domain name referenced by *name, unescape it, and write it to dest. Advances *name to point to the next label. Returns dest.
requirements: name must be non-NULL and point to a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated domain name string.
dest must be a valid, writable buffer.
size must specify the capacity of dest in bytes and be sufficient to hold the unescaped label including the terminating NUL.
To be able to store any valid unescaped label, provide size >= AVAHI_LABEL_MAX (64).
*name is modified to point to the start of the next label in the original string.

functions.name: avahi_escape_label
functions.signature: char *avahi_escape_label(const char* src, size_t src_length, char **ret_name, size_t *ret_size);
functions.description: Escape a domain label from src (of length src_length) and write the escaped result to *ret_name, potentially updating the buffer and its size via *ret_size. Returns a pointer to the escaped string (typically *ret_name). Exact allocation and ownership semantics are not documented here.
requirements: src must be a valid pointer to at least src_length bytes of the label to escape (not necessarily NUL-terminated).
ret_name must be non-NULL; on success it will reference a buffer containing the escaped label.
ret_size must be non-NULL; it should indicate the current capacity of *ret_name on input and may be updated to the new capacity on output (exact contract is not documented).
Memory ownership and required deallocation of *ret_name are unknown from this header; consult implementation—do not assume standard free() vs avahi_free().

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_service_type_generic
functions.description: Validate that t is a generic DNS-SD service type, defined as a series of words starting with an underscore (e.g., _http._tcp). Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_service_type_strict
functions.description: Validate that t is a strict DNS-SD service type consisting of exactly two labels, with the second being _udp or _tcp. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_service_subtype
functions.description: Validate that t is a DNS-SD service subtype. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.
Exact subtype syntax rules beyond being a DNS-SD subtype are not detailed here.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_domain_name
functions.description: Validate that t is a syntactically valid domain name. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.
Maximum fully escaped domain string length is AVAHI_DOMAIN_NAME_MAX (1014); typical DNS limit for FQDN is 255 bytes (RFC1034), but exact enforcement here is not detailed.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_service_name
functions.description: Validate that t is a valid DNS-SD service instance name. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.
Exact character and length constraints are not detailed here.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_host_name
functions.description: Validate that t is a valid non-FQDN host name (i.e., without dots). Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
The name must not contain dots to be considered a non-FQDN host name.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.

functions.name: avahi_is_valid_fqdn
functions.description: Validate that t is a valid fully qualified domain name (FQDN) with more than one label and non-numerical. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise. Since 0.6.9.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string.
The FQDN must have more than one label and must be non-numerical.
Return value is 1 for valid, 0 for invalid.

functions.name: avahi_service_name_join
functions.signature: int avahi_service_name_join(char *p, size_t size, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain);
functions.description: Construct a complete DNS-SD service name from a service instance name, a service type, and a domain, writing the result into the provided buffer p.
requirements: p must be a valid, writable buffer.
size must specify the capacity of p in bytes and be large enough to hold the resulting service name including the terminating NUL.
name, type, and domain must be valid NUL-terminated C strings.
Return value semantics (e.g., 0 on success, negative on error) are not documented here.

functions.name: avahi_service_name_split
functions.signature: int avahi_service_name_split(const char *p, char *name, size_t name_size, char *type, size_t type_size, char *domain, size_t domain_size);
functions.description: Split a full DNS-SD service name into its components: service instance name, service type, and domain, writing each into the provided buffers.
requirements: p must be a valid NUL-terminated C string containing a full DNS-SD service name.
name, type, and domain must be valid, writable buffers sized by name_size, type_size, and domain_size, respectively.
Each size must be large enough to hold the corresponding component including the terminating NUL.
Return value semantics (e.g., success/error codes) are not documented here.

functions.name: avahi_get_type_from_subtype
functions.description: Given a DNS-SD subtype string, return a pointer to the type section (e.g., input '_foo._sub._bar._tcp' yields pointer to '_bar._tcp'). The returned pointer refers into the original string.
requirements: t must be a valid NUL-terminated C string representing a DNS-SD subtype.
The returned pointer aliases the input buffer; the input must outlive any use of the returned pointer.
If t does not contain a recognizable subtype pattern, the behavior or return value is not documented here (could be NULL or some part of t; unknown).

functions.name: avahi_malloc
functions.description: Allocates a new memory block, analogous to libc malloc(). Intended to be paired with avahi_free() and other Avahi allocation helpers.
requirements: Callers should free the returned memory with avahi_free() or via the active AvahiAllocator free() if a custom allocator is set.
Size is a byte count; behavior for size == 0 follows the underlying allocator (unspecified here).
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred from malloc-like behavior).

functions.name: avahi_malloc0
functions.description: Allocates a new memory block like avahi_malloc() but initializes the memory to zero (calloc-like).
requirements: Callers should free the returned memory with avahi_free().
Size is a byte count; behavior for size == 0 follows the underlying allocator (unspecified).
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_free
functions.description: Frees memory previously allocated by Avahi allocation routines (e.g., avahi_malloc, avahi_malloc0, avahi_realloc, avahi_strdup*).
requirements: The pointer p must have been obtained from Avahi’s allocator (default or custom set via avahi_set_allocator).
Do not pass pointers not allocated by the matching allocator.
Passing NULL is assumed to be a no-op as with libc free(), but not explicitly documented.

functions.name: avahi_realloc
functions.description: Resizes a previously allocated memory block, analogous to libc realloc(). Intended to be used with Avahi allocation routines.
requirements: If p is non-NULL, it must have been allocated by Avahi’s allocator (default or the one set via avahi_set_allocator).
The returned pointer should be freed with avahi_free().
Behavior for p == NULL and/or size == 0 follows realloc-like semantics but is not explicitly specified here.
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_new_internal
functions.signature: static inline void *avahi_new_internal(unsigned n, size_t k);
functions.description: Internal helper used by the avahi_new() macro to allocate an array of n elements of size k bytes using avahi_malloc(). Performs a checked multiplication to avoid overflow in debug builds.
requirements: Requires n < INT_MAX / k; the function asserts this condition (assert will abort on violation in debug builds).
On success returns a pointer to n*k bytes; caller must free with avahi_free().
k is expected to be a valid element size (typically sizeof(type)); n is the element count.
May return NULL if allocation fails (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_new0_internal
functions.signature: static inline void *avahi_new0_internal(unsigned n, size_t k);
functions.description: Internal helper used by the avahi_new0() macro to allocate and zero-initialize an array of n elements of size k bytes using avahi_malloc0(). Performs a checked multiplication to avoid overflow in debug builds.
requirements: Requires n < INT_MAX / k; the function asserts this condition (assert will abort on violation in debug builds).
On success returns a pointer to zeroed n*k bytes; caller must free with avahi_free().
k is expected to be a valid element size; n is the element count.
May return NULL if allocation fails (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_strdup
functions.description: Duplicates a C string, analogous to libc strdup(), allocating the copy via Avahi’s allocator. Free the result with avahi_free().
requirements: s must point to a NUL-terminated string; passing NULL is not valid (inferred from strdup semantics).
The returned string must be freed with avahi_free().
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_strndup
functions.description: Duplicates up to l bytes from the C string s, analogous to libc strndup(), allocating via Avahi’s allocator and NUL-terminating the result. Free the result with avahi_free().
requirements: s must point to a readable buffer of at least min(strlen(s), l) bytes; passing NULL is not valid (inferred from strndup semantics).
l is the maximum number of characters to copy; result is NUL-terminated.
The returned string must be freed with avahi_free().
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_memdup
functions.description: Duplicates a memory block of length l into a newly allocated buffer using avahi_malloc().
requirements: s must point to a readable memory region of at least l bytes; passing NULL with l > 0 is invalid (inferred from memdup semantics).
The returned buffer must be freed with avahi_free().
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_set_allocator
functions.description: Installs a custom allocator by providing function pointers for malloc/free/realloc/calloc. Passing NULL restores the default libc-based allocator. The AvahiAllocator structure is not copied and must remain valid for as long as it is in use.
requirements: a may be NULL to revert to default allocators.
If a is non-NULL, the AvahiAllocator object and its function pointers must remain valid after the call; the structure is not copied.
Provided functions must match the semantics and signatures of their libc counterparts; calloc may be NULL (documented), others should be non-NULL.
Do not free memory with a different allocator than the one that allocated it; callers must ensure consistent use after changing the allocator.
Thread-safety or reentrancy requirements are not documented; callers should ensure no concurrent allocations are in flight during a change (not specified, caution).

functions.name: avahi_strdup_printf
functions.description: Like sprintf(), formats according to fmt and arguments, but returns the result in a newly allocated buffer. Free with avahi_free().
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string; corresponding arguments must match the format specifiers.
The returned string must be freed with avahi_free().
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_strdup_vprintf
functions.description: va_list-based variant of avahi_strdup_printf(): formats according to fmt and ap and returns a newly allocated string. Free with avahi_free().
requirements: fmt must be a valid printf-style format string.
ap must be a properly initialized va_list for the specified fmt.
The returned string must be freed with avahi_free().
May return NULL on allocation failure (inferred).

functions.name: AvahiPoll::watch_new
functions.signature: AvahiWatch* (*watch_new)(const AvahiPoll *api, int fd, AvahiWatchEvent event, AvahiWatchCallback callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Create a new I/O watch for the specified file descriptor and events. The implementation will invoke the provided callback whenever any of the requested events occurs on the file descriptor. Intended for integrating Avahi with an external main loop using a poll(2)-like abstraction.
requirements: api must be a valid, initialized AvahiPoll vtable provided by the main-loop integration.
fd must be a valid open file descriptor.
event must specify one or more events from AvahiWatchEvent (AVAHI_WATCH_IN, AVAHI_WATCH_OUT, AVAHI_WATCH_ERR, AVAHI_WATCH_HUP).
callback must be a valid (non-NULL) function pointer of type AvahiWatchCallback; it will be called when events occur.
userdata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints.
The returned AvahiWatch must be released with watch_free() when no longer needed.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::watch_update
functions.description: Update the set of events being watched for an existing I/O watch. Safe to call from within an AvahiWatchCallback.
requirements: w must be a valid AvahiWatch previously created by watch_new() and not yet freed.
event must specify the new event mask using AVAHI_WATCH_* flags.
May be invoked from inside the AvahiWatchCallback for the same watch.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::watch_get_events
functions.description: Return the events that occurred for the specified watch. Safe to call from within an AvahiWatchCallback.
requirements: w must be a valid AvahiWatch previously created by watch_new() and not yet freed.
May be invoked from inside the AvahiWatchCallback for the same watch.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::watch_free
functions.description: Free and deregister an I/O watch. Safe to call from within an AvahiWatchCallback.
requirements: w must be a valid AvahiWatch previously created by watch_new() and not yet freed.
After calling watch_free(), the AvahiWatch pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.
May be invoked from inside the AvahiWatchCallback for the same watch.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::timeout_new
functions.signature: AvahiTimeout* (*timeout_new)(const AvahiPoll *api, const struct timeval *tv, AvahiTimeoutCallback callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Create a new timeout that will trigger at the specified absolute time. If tv is NULL, the timeout is created in a disabled state. When the timeout expires, the callback is called and the timeout is automatically disabled; it can be re-enabled via timeout_update().
requirements: api must be a valid, initialized AvahiPoll vtable provided by the main-loop integration.
tv must point to an absolute expiration time (struct timeval, typically gettimeofday epoch); if NULL, the timeout starts disabled.
callback must be a valid (non-NULL) function pointer of type AvahiTimeoutCallback.
userdata is an opaque pointer passed back to the callback; no constraints.
The returned AvahiTimeout must be released with timeout_free() when no longer needed.
After firing, the timeout becomes disabled and must be re-armed with timeout_update() to trigger again.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::timeout_update
functions.description: Update the absolute expiration time for an existing timeout; passing NULL disables it. Safe to call from within an AvahiTimeoutCallback.
requirements: The AvahiTimeout pointer must refer to a valid timeout previously created by timeout_new() and not yet freed.
tv must point to the new absolute expiration time; if NULL, the timeout is disabled.
May be invoked from inside the AvahiTimeoutCallback for the same timeout.

functions.name: AvahiPoll::timeout_free
functions.description: Free and deregister a timeout. Safe to call from within an AvahiTimeoutCallback.
requirements: t must be a valid AvahiTimeout previously created by timeout_new() and not yet freed.
After calling timeout_free(), the AvahiTimeout pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.
May be invoked from inside the AvahiTimeoutCallback for the same timeout.

functions.name: avahi_timeval_compare
functions.signature: int avahi_timeval_compare(const struct timeval *a, const struct timeval *b);
functions.description: Compares two timeval instances. Returns a negative value if a < b, 0 if a == b, and a positive value otherwise. Useful for ordering or equality checks on absolute times.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval.
b must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval.
The function does not modify the input timevals.

functions.name: avahi_timeval_diff
functions.signature: AvahiUsec avahi_timeval_diff(const struct timeval *a, const struct timeval *b);
functions.description: Computes the difference between two timeval instances and returns it as microseconds (AvahiUsec, signed 64-bit). Typically interpreted as a - b (details beyond this are not explicitly documented).
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval.
b must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval.
Result is a signed 64-bit microsecond value; callers should handle potential negative values and range limits of int64_t.

functions.name: avahi_timeval_add
functions.signature: struct timeval* avahi_timeval_add(struct timeval *a, AvahiUsec usec);
functions.description: Adds the specified number of microseconds to the given timeval and returns the pointer to it. The input timeval *a is modified in-place.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval.
usec is a signed 64-bit microsecond offset (AvahiUsec); callers should ensure that adding usec does not overflow/underflow struct timeval fields (behavior not specified if it would).
The returned pointer is the same as the input pointer a.

functions.name: avahi_age
functions.description: Returns the difference between the current time and the given time a, in microseconds. The result is positive if a is earlier than now, negative if a is in the future.
requirements: a must be a non-null pointer to a valid, initialized struct timeval representing an absolute time.
Callers should be prepared for negative results if a is in the future and for potential 64-bit range limits.

functions.name: avahi_elapse_time
functions.signature: struct timeval *avahi_elapse_time(struct timeval *tv, unsigned ms, unsigned j);
functions.description: Fills tv with the current time plus ms milliseconds plus an extra jitter of up to j milliseconds. Pass 0 for j to disable jitter. Returns tv. Distribution and exact jitter behavior are not specified.
requirements: tv must be a non-null pointer to a writable struct timeval.
ms is an unsigned millisecond offset; callers should ensure values are within reasonable bounds to avoid overflow when converted to timeval.
j is an unsigned maximum jitter in milliseconds; set j to 0 to add no jitter.
The returned pointer is the same as the input pointer tv.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_new
functions.description: Creates a new AvahiSimplePoll main loop object. Intended for small test/example applications needing a poll()-based loop.
requirements: No arguments required.
Caller owns the returned AvahiSimplePoll* and must free it with avahi_simple_poll_free().
Returned pointer may be NULL on allocation failure; caller should check for NULL before use.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_free
functions.description: Frees a previously created AvahiSimplePoll main loop object and releases its resources.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll* obtained from avahi_simple_poll_new().
Do not use s after this call (pointer becomes invalid).
Passing NULL is unspecified in the header; behavior is unknown.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_get
functions.description: Returns the AvahiPoll API vtable associated with this main loop. The same pointer is returned on each call. Useful for integrating components that expect an AvahiPoll implementation.
requirements: s must be a valid, initialized AvahiSimplePoll*.
Do not free or modify the returned AvahiPoll; it is owned by the AvahiSimplePoll instance and remains valid as long as s is valid.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_iterate
functions.description: Runs a single iteration of the simple poll main loop. Blocks and dispatches events according to sleep_time: <0 blocks until an event, 0 is non-blocking (poll-only), >0 blocks up to the specified milliseconds. Returns -1 on error, 0 on success with no quit requested, and 1 if a quit was scheduled.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
sleep_time may be negative, zero, or positive per the documented semantics.
Caller should handle return values: -1 indicates error; 1 indicates a scheduled quit; 0 indicates normal iteration.
Typically called in a loop until a non-zero value is returned.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_quit
functions.description: Requests that the main loop quits. Causes the next avahi_simple_poll_iterate() call to return 1.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Has effect on the next iterate; does not forcibly terminate a currently blocking iterate call unless the implementation supports wakeup separately.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_set_func
functions.description: Replaces the internally used poll() function for this main loop instance. By default, the system poll() is used. The provided function is called with the same parameters as poll, plus the supplied userdata.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
func must be a function compatible with AvahiPollFunc: int (*)(struct pollfd *ufds, unsigned int nfds, int timeout, void *userdata).
userdata is opaque and will be passed to func as provided.
Behavior when func is NULL is not documented; caller should not pass NULL unless the specific implementation documents it.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_prepare
functions.description: First stage of a manual iteration sequence equivalent to avahi_simple_poll_iterate(). Low-level API intended for advanced use. Prepares the polling state with the given timeout.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Intended to be followed by avahi_simple_poll_run() and then avahi_simple_poll_dispatch() as a single logical iteration.
Use only if you fully understand the internal iteration stages; details beyond order are not documented in this header.
timeout is an integer timeout parameter; exact effect beyond being part of preparation is not further documented.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_run
functions.description: Second stage of the manual iteration sequence corresponding to avahi_simple_poll_iterate(). Performs the blocking/polling step using the currently configured poll function.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Should be called after a successful avahi_simple_poll_prepare() and before avahi_simple_poll_dispatch().
Return value semantics are not documented here; treat non-zero as potential indication of quit/error consistent with iterate semantics when integrating.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_dispatch
functions.description: Third and final stage of the manual iteration sequence corresponding to avahi_simple_poll_iterate(). Dispatches any ready events and their callbacks.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Should be called after avahi_simple_poll_run() within the same logical iteration.
Return value semantics are not explicitly documented here; infer that non-zero may indicate quit or error consistent with iterate semantics.

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_loop
functions.description: Continuously calls avahi_simple_poll_iterate() in a loop until it returns a non-zero value, then returns that value to the caller. Provides a simple main loop runner.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Function may block indefinitely until a quit is requested or an error occurs.
Caller should handle the returned non-zero value: 1 indicates a quit was scheduled; -1 indicates error (per iterate semantics).

functions.name: avahi_simple_poll_wakeup
functions.description: Wakes up the main loop, primarily for threaded environments where another thread needs to interrupt a blocking poll.
requirements: s must be a valid AvahiSimplePoll*.
Intended to be safe for use from other threads to interrupt a blocking wait; specific threading guarantees beyond this note are not detailed in the header.

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_new
functions.description: Create a new threaded main-loop object. Allocates the internal AvahiSimplePoll but does not start the helper thread. Use avahi_threaded_poll_start() to run it and avahi_threaded_poll_free() to destroy it. Return value semantics (NULL on failure vs. other) are not documented here; callers should check the return for success before use.
requirements: Must be called before any other function that operates on an AvahiThreadedPoll instance.
Caller should check the returned pointer before use (return-on-failure behavior is not documented in this header).
The created object is not running until avahi_threaded_poll_start() is called.

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_free
functions.description: Free a threaded main-loop object. If the helper thread is running, this call stops it and releases all associated resources.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll previously created by avahi_threaded_poll_new().
Do not use p after this call returns.
Behavior for p == NULL is not documented here (unknown).
If the helper thread was started, this call will stop it before freeing (per header comment).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_get
functions.description: Return the AvahiPoll API object associated with this threaded event loop. The same pointer is returned on every call for a given AvahiThreadedPoll. Intended for creating and managing event sources that plug into the AvahiSimplePoll run by the helper thread.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll.
The returned AvahiPoll pointer remains valid only as long as p remains valid; do not free it yourself.
The same pointer is returned on repeated calls for the same p (per header comment).
Access to the returned AvahiPoll and associated objects must be synchronized after the helper thread has been started (use avahi_threaded_poll_lock()/unlock()).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_start
functions.description: Start the helper thread that runs the internal AvahiSimplePoll. After the thread starts, all access to the event loop object, the AvahiPoll, and its associated objects must be synchronized (e.g., using avahi_threaded_poll_lock()/unlock()). Event callbacks are invoked from the helper thread with the lock already held, so calls to lock within those callbacks are not required.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll created by avahi_threaded_poll_new().
After this returns successfully, all external access to the event loop, AvahiPoll, and associated objects must be synchronized using avahi_threaded_poll_lock()/unlock().
Do not call avahi_threaded_poll_lock() from within event callbacks, since callbacks are executed with the lock already held (per header comment).
Return value/error conventions are not documented here; callers should check the int return and handle failure appropriately (semantics unknown).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_stop
functions.description: Request that the event loop quits and the associated helper thread stops. Intended to be called from outside the helper thread to shut it down.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll whose helper thread may be running.
Call this from outside the helper thread (per header comment).
Return value/error conventions are not documented here; callers should check the int return and handle failure appropriately (semantics unknown).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_quit
functions.description: Request that the event loop quits and the associated helper thread stops. Intended to be called from within the helper thread.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll.
Call this from inside the helper thread (per header comment).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_lock
functions.description: Lock the threaded main-loop object. Use this to synchronize access to the event loop and its objects (e.g., when creating event sources) from threads other than the helper thread. Event callbacks are invoked from the helper thread with this lock already held.
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll.
Use when accessing event loop objects from any thread other than the helper thread (per header comment).
Do not call from event callbacks, as those are executed with the lock already held (per header comment).
Must be paired with a corresponding avahi_threaded_poll_unlock() by the same thread; reentrancy/recursion semantics are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: avahi_threaded_poll_unlock
functions.description: Unlock the threaded main-loop object. Counterpart to avahi_threaded_poll_lock().
requirements: p must be a valid AvahiThreadedPoll.
Must only be called after a successful avahi_threaded_poll_lock() on the same object by the calling thread.
Use as the counterpart to avahi_threaded_poll_lock() (per header comment).

functions.name: avahi_strerror
functions.description: Returns a human-readable string describing the given Avahi error code. Typical usage is to pass an error value from the AVAHI_OK/AVAHI_ERR_* enumeration defined in this header to obtain a displayable message (e.g., for logs or user feedback). The returned pointer refers to an internal constant string; use it read-only.
requirements: The error argument should be an Avahi error code (AVAHI_OK or one of the AVAHI_ERR_* values) defined in this header; behavior for other integers is unspecified.
The returned const char* points to read-only storage; the caller must not modify or free it.
The function may be called at any time with any error code; no object state is required.

functions.name: avahi_rlist_prepend
functions.description: Prepends a new node holding the given data pointer to the beginning (head) of an AvahiRList and returns the new head. Typical usage: update your head pointer with the returned value. Implementation details such as node allocation and whether the function ever copies or takes ownership of data are not documented in this header; assume it stores the pointer as-is.
requirements: r must be a valid AvahiRList head pointer or NULL (inference based on common list prepend semantics; not explicitly stated).
data is an arbitrary pointer stored in the node; no ownership transfer or lifetime rules are documented (unknown).
The caller should use the returned pointer as the new list head; prior head becomes the second element if non-NULL (inference).
Thread-safety is not documented; callers should synchronize externally if the list may be accessed concurrently (unknown).

functions.name: avahi_rlist_remove
functions.description: Removes the first occurrence of a node whose data matches the given pointer from the list and returns the (possibly new) head. Use when you know the data pointer and want to delete its first match. Matching semantics are not specified here, but in typical implementations this is pointer equality on the stored void*.
requirements: r must be a valid AvahiRList head pointer or NULL (inference based on common list semantics; not explicitly stated).
data is the target pointer to match against node->data; matching is likely by pointer equality (inference; not explicitly stated).
The caller must replace the head with the returned value to keep the list consistent, especially when removing the first element (inference).
Behavior when data is not found is not specified; typical behavior is to return the original head (unknown exact behavior).
No guarantees are provided about freeing or touching the pointed-to payload; only the list node is expected to be affected (unknown).
Thread-safety is not documented; callers should synchronize externally if the list may be accessed concurrently (unknown).

functions.name: avahi_rlist_remove_by_link
functions.description: Removes the specified node (link) n from the list r and returns the (possibly new) head. Use when you already have a pointer to the list node to be removed.
requirements: r must be a valid AvahiRList head pointer or NULL (inference; not explicitly stated).
n should be a valid node that belongs to the list headed by r and must not be NULL (inference from the function name and signature; not explicitly stated).
The caller must use the returned pointer as the new head to reflect potential head removal (inference).
Behavior when n does not belong to r is not specified; passing a mismatched node may result in undefined behavior (unknown).
No guarantees are provided about freeing or touching the node->data payload; only the list link is expected to be removed (unknown).
Thread-safety is not documented; callers should synchronize externally if the list may be accessed concurrently (unknown).

functions.name: avahi_client_new
functions.signature: AvahiClient* avahi_client_new(const AvahiPoll *poll_api, AvahiClientFlags flags, AvahiClientCallback callback, void *userdata, int *error);
functions.description: Creates a new AvahiClient instance bound to the provided event loop API. Optionally invokes a state-change callback (which may be NULL) during construction; note the callback is called for the first time from within avahi_client_new(). If AVAHI_CLIENT_NO_FAIL is set and the daemon is unavailable, the client enters AVAHI_CLIENT_CONNECTING and later transitions when the daemon appears. On failure, returns NULL and (optionally) stores an error code in *error. Typical usage: construct with a valid AvahiPoll implementation, handle initial callback invocation carefully, check for NULL return and inspect *error if provided, and free with avahi_client_free when done.
requirements: poll_api must point to a valid AvahiPoll implementation compatible with the process event loop (inferred from parameter purpose).
flags is a bitmask of AvahiClientFlags; recognized values include AVAHI_CLIENT_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG and AVAHI_CLIENT_NO_FAIL (from header docs).

callback may be NULL. If non-NULL, it will be called at least once from within avahi_client_new(); it must not assume global variables have been initialized after the call site; use the AvahiClient pointer passed to the callback rather than any global pointer (stated in comments).
userdata is passed verbatim to callback; no lifetime guarantees beyond what the caller provides (inferred).
error may be NULL. If non-NULL and creation fails (function returns NULL), *error will contain the failure cause (stated).
Caller must check the return value for NULL before using the client (inferred from return-on-failure behavior).
If AVAHI_CLIENT_NO_FAIL is set, the initial state may be AVAHI_CLIENT_CONNECTING; caller must be prepared to handle deferred connection (stated).
The returned AvahiClient must be released with avahi_client_free; all objects created from it become invalid after free (stated under avahi_client_free).

functions.name: avahi_client_free
functions.description: Frees an AvahiClient instance and automatically frees all associated browser, resolver, and entry group objects. After this call, any pointers to those objects (and the client) become invalid.
requirements: client must be a valid AvahiClient previously returned by avahi_client_new (inferred).
After calling this function, all associated browser/resolve/entry group objects are invalid and must not be used (stated).
Do not use the client pointer after this call (inferred).

functions.name: avahi_client_get_host_name

functions.signature: AvahiDomainBrowser* avahi_domain_browser_new(AvahiClient *client, AvahiIfIndex interface, AvahiProtocol protocol, const char *domain, AvahiDomainBrowserType btype, AvahiLookupFlags flags, AvahiDomainBrowserCallback callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Creates a domain browser that discovers domains on the local network and reports results via the provided callback. Typical usage: create with a connected AvahiClient, optionally specifying interface/protocol/domain filtering, then handle AvahiBrowserEvent callbacks until you no longer need it and free the browser.
requirements: client should be a valid AvahiClient pointer (state requirements are not specified in this header).
interface may be a specific interface or AVAHI_IF_UNSPEC to browse on all interfaces (implied by similar API notes; explicit requirement not stated here).
protocol may be AVAHI_PROTO_INET, AVAHI_PROTO_INET6, or AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC to control query transport (not further specified here).
domain may be NULL to use the default browsing domain (usually .local) is not explicitly stated for this API; value constraints unknown.
callback is invoked with AvahiDomainBrowser events; whether NULL is permitted is unknown.
The returned AvahiDomainBrowser must be freed with avahi_domain_browser_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: avahi_domain_browser_get_client
functions.description: Returns the AvahiClient that owns the specified AvahiDomainBrowser. Useful to retrieve the parent client from the browser instance.

functions.description: Cleans up and frees an AvahiDomainBrowser object. After this call, the browser pointer must not be used.
requirements: The pointer must have been obtained from avahi_domain_browser_new and not yet freed.

functions.description: Creates a browser for DNS-SD services of a given type and domain. The callback is invoked when services appear or are removed. Events may be collapsed to minimize traffic; subscribe to changes using avahi_service_resolver_new if you need continuous updates to service data.
requirements: client must be a valid AvahiClient pointer.
interface: In most cases pass AVAHI_IF_UNSPEC to browse on all interfaces (as documented).
protocol: In most cases pass AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC to browse via both IPv4 and IPv6 (as documented).
type must be a service type string such as "_http._tcp".
domain may be NULL to use the default browsing domain (usually ".local") (as documented).
callback is required to receive browse events; whether NULL is allowed is not documented.
The returned AvahiServiceBrowser must be freed with avahi_service_browser_free when no longer needed.
Event collapsing means a removed/new pair for the same service may be suppressed; do not assume every change emits both events.

functions.name: avahi_service_browser_get_client

requirements: The AvahiServiceBrowser pointer must be valid and not yet freed.

functions.name: avahi_service_browser_free
functions.description: Frees a service browser and releases associated resources. After freeing, the browser must not be used.
requirements: The pointer must have been created by avahi_service_browser_new and not previously freed.

requirements: client should be a valid AvahiClient pointer.

functions.name: avahi_service_type_browser_get_client

functions.name: avahi_service_type_browser_free
functions.description: Frees an AvahiServiceTypeBrowser and releases its resources.
requirements: The pointer must refer to an existing AvahiServiceTypeBrowser created by avahi_service_type_browser_new and not yet freed.
Do not access the browser after this call. Return value semantics are not specified.

functions.name: avahi_service_resolver_new
functions.signature: AvahiServiceResolver* avahi_service_resolver_new(AvahiClient *client, AvahiIfIndex interface, AvahiProtocol protocol, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain, AvahiProtocol aprotocol, AvahiLookupFlags flags, AvahiServiceResolverCallback callback, void *userdata);
functions.description: Creates a resolver for a specific service instance to obtain its target host, address, port, and TXT data. The interface/protocol/name/type/domain should match the values received from AvahiServiceBrowserCallback. The protocol parameter controls the query transport (UDP/IPv4 vs UDP/IPv6), while aprotocol selects the desired address family (A vs AAAA). See the detailed notes for UNSPEC behavior: resolvers given UNSPEC as query protocol default to INET6; UNSPEC as address protocol resolves to an address matching the query protocol. On typical daemons, all combinations resolve except INET addresses via INET6 queries due to publish-* settings.
requirements: client must be a valid AvahiClient pointer.
interface must be the interface value received in AvahiServiceBrowserCallback for the target service (as documented).
protocol must be the protocol value received in AvahiServiceBrowserCallback for the target service (as documented; AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC is not delivered in callbacks).
name, type, and domain must be exactly those from the corresponding AvahiServiceBrowserCallback for the target service (as documented).
aprotocol specifies the desired address family; pass AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC if the application can handle both IPv4 and IPv6 (as documented).
Be aware of UNSPEC defaults: a resolver with UNSPEC/UNSPEC behaves like INET6/INET6 (as documented).
The callback receives AvahiResolverEvent notifications with resolved data; whether a NULL callback is allowed is not documented.
The returned AvahiServiceResolver must be freed with avahi_service_resolver_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: avahi_service_resolver_get_client
functions.description: Returns the AvahiClient owning the specified AvahiServiceResolver.
requirements: The AvahiServiceResolver pointer must point to a valid, live resolver.

functions.name: avahi_service_resolver_free
functions.description: Frees a service resolver and releases its resources. After this call the resolver must not be used.
requirements: The resolver pointer must have been created by avahi_service_resolver_new and not yet freed.
Return value semantics are not documented here.

functions.description: Creates a resolver to resolve a host name to an address (A/AAAA) on a given interface/protocol, delivering results via the callback.

name must be the host name to resolve.
aprotocol selects the desired address family (IPv4/IPv6) or AVAHI_PROTO_UNSPEC to accept either.
Callback receives AvahiResolverEvent and result data; NULL-ability is not documented.
The returned resolver must be freed with avahi_host_name_resolver_free.

functions.description: Returns the AvahiClient associated with an AvahiAddressResolver.

functions.description: Creates a browser for DNS records of a given name/class/type on the local network and reports results via the callback.
requirements: client should be a valid AvahiClient pointer.
interface/protocol select the interface and transport; UNSPEC usage is typical but not detailed here.
name is the owner name to browse (FQDN-style string).
clazz is the DNS class (e.g., AVAHI_DNS_CLASS_IN); valid values are not enumerated here.
type is the DNS RR type (e.g., AVAHI_DNS_TYPE_TXT, SRV, etc.); valid values are not enumerated here.
callback receives AvahiBrowserEvent notifications with record data; NULL-ability is not documented.

functions.description: Returns the AvahiClient associated with an AvahiRecordBrowser.
requirements: The AvahiRecordBrowser pointer must be valid and not freed.

functions.description: Create a new AvahiEntryGroup associated with the given AvahiClient and a user-supplied callback. The callback is invoked on entry-group state changes and is called at least once during construction (inside avahi_entry_group_new). requirements: callback must not be NULL.
The callback may be invoked from within avahi_entry_group_new before it returns; do not rely on globals set after the call to be initialized during that first callback.
When handling the first callback, prefer using the AvahiEntryGroup* passed to the callback rather than any global you intend to store it in.
c must refer to a valid, initialized AvahiClient.

functions.name: avahi_entry_group_free
functions.description: Clean up and free an AvahiEntryGroup object and its resources.

Do not use the AvahiEntryGroup pointer after this call (use-after-free).

functions.name: avahi_entry_group_reset
functions.description: Reset an AvahiEntryGroup, withdrawing its current entries immediately so it can be reused to add/commit new entries.

functions.name: avahi_entry_group_add_service
functions.signature: int avahi_entry_group_add_service(AvahiEntryGroup *group, AvahiIfIndex interface, AvahiProtocol protocol, AvahiPublishFlags flags, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain, const char *host, uint16_t port, ...) AVAHI_GCC_SENTINEL;
functions.description: Add a DNS-SD service to the entry group. TXT records are supplied as a NULL-terminated varargs list of const char* strings. The service is not announced until avahi_entry_group_commit is called.
requirements: group must be a valid AvahiEntryGroup.
name must be a valid service instance name: non-NULL, valid UTF-8, length < 63 characters.
type must be non-NULL (e.g., "_http._tcp").
domain may be NULL to let the daemon choose.
host may be NULL to use the local host name.
flags is usually 0 unless a specific publish flag is required.
The variable arguments for TXT records must be a sequence of const char* entries terminated by a NULL sentinel.
port is a uint16_t and must contain the service port number.
The service will not be announced until avahi_entry_group_commit is called.

functions.description: Add a DNS-SD service to the entry group using an AvahiStringList for TXT records. The service is not announced until commit. The provided AvahiStringList is not retained by the library and may be freed after the call returns.
requirements: group must be a valid AvahiEntryGroup.
name must be non-NULL, valid UTF-8, and < 63 characters.
type must be non-NULL (e.g., "_http._tcp").
domain may be NULL; host may be NULL to use local hostname.
flags is usually 0 unless special behavior is desired.
txt may be freed by the caller after this function returns.
The service will not be announced until avahi_entry_group_commit is called.

functions.description: Add a DNS-SD subtype (e.g., "_printer._sub") to an existing service already present in the entry group. Multiple subtypes may be added for a single service.

interface should match the value used when the service was originally added.
protocol should match the value used when the service was originally added.
flags should remain 0 unless a specific, known behavior is required.

functions.signature: int avahi_entry_group_update_service_txt(AvahiEntryGroup *g, AvahiIfIndex interface, AvahiProtocol protocol, AvahiPublishFlags flags, const char *name, const char *type, const char *domain, ...) AVAHI_GCC_SENTINEL;

protocol should match the value used in the original add_service call.

a must point to a valid AvahiAddress instance describing the desired address.

functions.signature: int avahi_entry_group_add_record(AvahiEntryGroup *group, AvahiIfIndex interface, AvahiProtocol protocol, AvahiPublishFlags flags, const char *name, uint16_t clazz, uint16_t type, uint32_t ttl, const void *rdata, size_t size);
